prompt:
Write 12 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a side impact at intersection claim, in time order. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1174; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- Records show long-standing treatment for the same condition before the crash; most of the current complaints come from it.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: The claim was reported by the claimant after a side impact at an intersection. The driver is named on the policy, and the coverage was in force at the time of the loss.

Entry 2: Police attended the scene and confirmed the claimant was in the vehicle that was struck. The claimant reported neck and back pain at the scene.

Entry 3: I obtained the other driver's statement, which matches the claimant's description of the collision. The other driver stated that the light had turned in the claimant's favor.

Entry 4: Witnesses who spoke with me gave accounts consistent with the claimant's version of how the accident happened. Scene photographs were also reviewed and are in the file.

Entry 5: The damage to the claimant's vehicle is on the driver's side and lines up with the direction and force of the impact described. No earlier damage to the vehicle is known from our records or the repair inspection.

Entry 6: I found nothing suggesting the damage occurred before the coverage start date. The vehicle's history was checked and shows no prior claims on this area.

Entry 7: The claimant was seen at an urgent care facility the same day and was diagnosed with neck and back strain. Treatment at that stage was consistent with the kind of force involved in a side impact.

Entry 8: I spoke with the claimant the following week, and the account of the accident was the same as in the first report. The claimant has given the same description in every conversation since.

Entry 9: The claimant's treating provider requested authorization for physical therapy over several weeks. The course of care was typical for this injury, and the number of visits tapered as the claimant improved.

Entry 10: Medical records were requested from the prior treating provider. These show long-standing treatment for the same neck and back condition before this accident, and most of the current complaints appear to relate to that earlier condition.

Entry 11: I discussed the prior records with the treating provider, who agreed that the current injury is a real strain from the crash but that the ongoing symptoms are largely the pre-existing condition. The claim is being evaluated with that distinction in mind.

Entry 12: The claimant is not represented by an attorney and has been informed of the coverage terms and the next steps. The file will be reviewed again once the final treatment report is received.
